record.paper_title: On Open Problems of Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalues Problem
record.original_question: Given an n x n entrywise nonnegative matrix A, must there exist an n x n invertible real matrix P such that the similar matrix B = P^{-1} A P is also entrywise nonnegative?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix with real entries, all of which are nonnegative. Determine whether there must exist an $n \times n$ invertible real matrix $P$, other than the identity (and not merely a permutation matrix or positive diagonal matrix or composition thereof), such that the similar matrix $B = P^{-1} A P$ also has all entries nonnegative. Equivalently, characterize those entrywise nonnegative matrices $A$ which admit a nontrivial real similarity that preserves entrywise nonnegativity.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this similarity-preserving-nonnegativity question was located in available sources; the broader nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem remains open in general, and specialized similarity questions of this type do not appear to have a definitive published answer.

status_evidence.title: Nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem
status_evidence.snippet: The nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem (NIEP) remains unsolved in general for n >= 5.
status_evidence.claim: Related broader problem is still open.
